items.text: While alive supervision is active, when a supervised task has not completed an execution for 2 consecutive periods of its own, the supervisor shall detect an alive fault with fault code 1.
The supervisor shall start alive supervision when the start-up integrity checks have passed.

When a supervised task has not started by the end of its late-start limit, counted from the release of that task and with a start delay equal to the limit counting as within the limit, the supervisor shall detect a late-start fault with fault code 2 no later than 100 µs after the limit expires.
items.rationale: Reworked in round 11 (F-sys-req-item-r11-001, -002). Boundary rule (CON-SUP-127): a start delay equal to the limit is within the limit, so a start at the limit is accepted and no fault is decided; the fault decision applies only to a task not started by the end of the limit, which removes the simultaneous expiry-and-start ambiguity. Detection window (CON-SUP-127, CON-SUP-128): detected when the limit expires, with the 100 µs measurement resolution of SYS-SUP-008 (CON-SUP-103) allowing detection up to 100 µs after expiry, now stated in the obligation. Verification uses margins of at least 200 µs either side of the limit (CON-SUP-127).

items.text: When the execution time of a supervised task, counted from the start of that execution, exceeds the execution limit of that task without a completion having been reported, the supervisor shall detect an overrun fault with fault code 3 no later than 100 µs after the limit expires, without waiting for the task to complete; an execution time equal to the limit is within the limit, so a completion reported at the instant the limit expires is accepted and is not an overrun.
items.rationale: Reworked for F-sys-req-item-r11-003 and F-sys-req-item-r11-004. Boundary rule (CON-SUP-127): a measured execution time equal to the limit is within the limit, so when completion and expiry coincide the completion wins and no fault is raised; an overrun exists only when the execution time exceeds the limit with no completion. Detection window (CON-SUP-103, CON-SUP-127): with the 100 µs measurement resolution, detection may occur up to 100 µs after expiry, and this is now stated in the obligation. Verification uses margins of at least 200 µs either side of the limit (CON-SUP-127). CON-SUP-105 counts the 50 ms reaction time from the instant the expiry makes the fault detectable. Earlier rework: F-sys-req-item-r2-002. CON-SUP-103 says an overrun is detected when the limit expires, and CON-SUP-105 makes the expiry of a timing limit the instant the fault becomes detectable. An execution longer than the limit is an overrun and an execution not longer than the limit is not, so a completion at or before expiry is accepted (CON-SUP-103). Updated for CON-SUP-127 (answer to former OP-SYS-009): an execution time equal to the limit is within the limit; because of the 100 µs resolution of SYS-SUP-008 a violation may be detected up to 100 µs after the limit expires, and verification uses margins of at least 200 µs either side of the limit.

items.text: At the end of each control cycle, when the checkpoints of the tasks released in that cycle have not arrived in the configured order or a checkpoint is missing, the supervisor shall detect a flow fault with fault code 4.

The supervisor shall read the set of supervised tasks, their periods, late-start limits, execution limits and checkpoint order from the configuration data, so that changing them requires no change to the supervisor code.

The supervisor shall supervise three 10 ms tasks T_IN, T_CTRL and T_OUT, released in that order every 10 ms, and the 100 ms task T_DIAG, released after T_OUT in every tenth 10 ms period, with default limits of a late start after 2 ms, an execution longer than 3 ms for each 10 ms task and an execution longer than 20 ms for T_DIAG.
The supervisor shall measure task start delays and execution times with a resolution of 100 µs.

When the configuration data at start-up contains a timing limit longer than the period of its task, a task period of zero, or an entry naming an unknown task (CON-SUP-115), the supervisor shall detect a configuration fault with fault code 9.
items.rationale: Reworked for F-sys-req-item-r2-003. Detection is kept here; the safe-state latch on fault code 9 is split into SYS-SUP-043 so each can be verified independently. Other items that cite SYS-SUP-009 for the latch (SYS-SUP-013, SYS-SUP-021, SYS-SUP-027, SYS-SUP-042) now find it in SYS-SUP-043.

items.text: When the independent watchdog, which runs from its own clock, has not been serviced for 100 ms, the controller shall perform a reset.

At the end of each control cycle, when no fault with fault code 1 to 7 or 9 has been detected since the last reset and the safe state is not latched, the supervisor shall refresh the window watchdog once.
items.rationale: Reworked for F-sys-req-item-r2-004. The refresh condition is now the exact complement of the withholding condition in SYS-SUP-013: SYS-SUP-013 withholds every watchdog service action from the detection of a fault with fault code 1 to 7 or 9 until the next reset and while the safe state is latched, so a cycle with no new detection that follows an earlier detection, or that occurs while the safe state is latched, gets no refresh. Both requirements use the same fault-code set, so they never demand opposite actions; the resulting missing refresh is handled by SYS-SUP-012 and SYS-SUP-010.

items.text: When the window watchdog is refreshed earlier than 6 ms or later than 12 ms after the previous refresh, the controller shall perform a reset.

From the detection of a fault with fault code 1 to 7 or 9 until the next reset, and while the safe state is latched, the supervisor shall withhold every watchdog service action, including the refresh of the window watchdog.
items.rationale: Reworked for CON-SUP-121 (answer to former OP-SYS-011): watchdog servicing stops at fault detection without exception, so withholding starts at the detection instant and no longer waits for completion of the fault report and safe-state entry. If a watchdog reset comes before they complete, the reset puts the outputs in the safe reset state (SYS-SUP-020) and the fault is reported at the next start-up as fault code 8 (SYS-SUP-032, SYS-SUP-026); the report of the fault being handled is then not required (SYS-SUP-023). Once withholding has started it persists until a reset, and while the safe state is latched (SYS-SUP-009, SYS-SUP-028, SYS-SUP-043) it persists across resets, which is the exact complement of the service conditions of SYS-SUP-011 and SYS-SUP-044. Fault code 8 is reported after a reset and is not a health condition of a running task. The resulting missing refresh ends in a reset through SYS-SUP-012 and SYS-SUP-010. While the latch is set, the withholding forces watchdog resets, the outputs are held in the safe state through each of them by SYS-SUP-046; the latch survives those resets (SYS-SUP-029) and ends only at a power-on reset (SYS-SUP-045).

items.text: Before releasing any task, the supervisor shall detect a code integrity fault at start-up with fault code 5 when the CRC-32 (polynomial 0x04C11DB7) computed over the program code between the linker symbols __app_start and __app_end differs from the reference value of 4 bytes stored at the linker symbol __app_crc, outside that range.
items.rationale: Updated for CON-SUP-124 (answer to former OP-SYS-004): same CRC-32 as the configuration block, reference at __app_crc. Rework r11 (F-sys-req-item-r11-005): CON-SUP-107 and CON-SUP-124 give only the polynomial 0x04C11DB7. The initial value, input and output reflection, final XOR and the byte order of the 4-byte reference at __app_crc are not given, and different choices yield different results for the same image. These are not invented here; they are recorded as blocking OP-SYS-014 and need a human decision before the expected result of this comparison can be determined. The same gap affects SYS-SUP-015 and SYS-SUP-019, which are not changed in this rework.

items.text: Before releasing any task, the supervisor shall detect a configuration integrity fault with fault code 6 when the CRC-32 (polynomial 0x04C11DB7) computed over the configuration data block differs from the CRC-32 stored with that block.
While the application runs, the supervisor shall check one 1 KiB segment of the program code in each control cycle.
The supervisor shall complete a full pass of the run-time program-code check of a 1 MiB image within 11 s.
The supervisor shall use at most 0.5 ms of processor time per control cycle for the run-time program-code check.

When the run-time program-code check completes a full pass over the program code and the CRC-32 (polynomial 0x04C11DB7) it computed differs from the reference value of 4 bytes stored at the linker symbol __app_crc, the supervisor shall detect a run-time code integrity fault with fault code 7.
items.rationale: Updated for CON-SUP-124 (answer to former OP-SYS-004): one CRC-32 reference value for the whole image, so the comparison is made per full pass; CON-SUP-105 makes the completion of the failing integrity computation the detectable instant. Rework r11 (F-sys-req-item-r11-006): the CRC initial value, input and output reflection, final XOR and the byte order of the 4-byte reference are not given by CON-SUP-107 or CON-SUP-124 and are not invented here. The missing parameters are already recorded as blocking decision OP-SYS-014 (no duplicate added); the expected comparison result of this item is unique only once OP-SYS-014 is answered by a person, and the text will then cite those parameters.

items.text: From any reset until the start-up integrity checks have passed, the controller shall hold both control outputs and the status signal low.

While the start-up integrity checks have passed, no fault with fault code 1 to 7 or 9 has been detected since the last reset and the safe state is not latched, the supervisor shall drive the status signal high.
items.rationale: Passing the start-up checks is a necessary but not sufficient condition for the high (operational) level of CON-SUP-109. A detected fault (SYS-SUP-022) or a latched safe state (SYS-SUP-009, SYS-SUP-028) takes precedence and keeps the status signal low until a power-on reset, so this requirement cannot override the latch. Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r2-013: the condition now uses the same since-the-last-reset wording as SYS-SUP-011, SYS-SUP-013 and SYS-SUP-044, so a fault that clears before the reset does not raise the status signal again. The status signal is low from the detection (SYS-SUP-022) until the next reset; after that reset SYS-SUP-020 holds it low until the start-up checks have passed, and only then, if the safe state is not latched, does this item raise it, which matches the recovery sequence of STK-SUP-010 and CON-SUP-110.

items.text: When a fault with fault code 1 to 7 or 9 is detected, the controller shall drive both control outputs low and the status signal low within 50 ms of the instant the fault becomes detectable by its rule.
items.rationale: The detectable instant is defined in CON-SUP-105 per fault class.

items.text: Unless a watchdog reset occurs first, the supervisor shall send the fault report on the diagnostic serial line within 10 ms of the detection of the fault.
items.rationale: CON-SUP-112 fixes the 10 ms deadline from detection. CON-SUP-120 makes the fault report and the safe-state entry (SYS-SUP-022) independent, in either order, so this item states only the 10 ms deadline from detection and takes no position on the order. Updated for CON-SUP-121: a watchdog reset that comes before the report completes removes the obligation for the fault being handled; that fault is reported at the next start-up as fault code 8 (SYS-SUP-032).

items.text: The supervisor shall send each fault report as the text line FLT,<code>,<entity>,<ms since start> terminated by a line feed.

The supervisor shall assign fault codes as follows: 1 alive, 2 late start, 3 overrun, 4 flow, 5 code integrity at start-up, 6 configuration integrity, 7 code integrity at run time, 8 watchdog reset, 9 configuration out of range.

The supervisor shall report the name of the affected task as entity for fault codes 1 to 3, the entity CODE for fault codes 5 and 7, the entity CONFIG for fault codes 6 and 9, and the entity IWDG or WWDG for fault code 8, according to the watchdog whose reset flag was set.
items.rationale: Extended for CON-SUP-119 (entities of fault codes 8 and 9). Reworked for F-sys-req-item-r5-004: codes 1 to 3 each concern one task (alive: the stopped task; late start and overrun: the task whose limit was violated), so the task name is unambiguous. Fault code 4 (flow) is stated separately in SYS-SUP-049 because a missing or out-of-order checkpoint can involve more than one task (CON-SUP-122).

items.text: When a fault with fault code 1 to 7 is detected and the detection does not latch the safe state, the supervisor shall request a software reset within 20 ms after the later of the completion of the fault report transmission and the completion of the safe-state entry.
items.rationale: Reworked for CON-SUP-120: the 20 ms counts from the later of report completion and safe-state entry, which are independent (SYS-SUP-022, SYS-SUP-023). Per CON-SUP-117 the first and second detections of the same fault code request a reset and the third latches the safe state without a reset (SYS-SUP-028, SYS-SUP-042). A configuration fault (fault code 9) latches at once (SYS-SUP-043) and requests no reset. Fault code 8 is reported after a reset and does not enter the safe state.

items.text: When a fault with fault code 1 to 7 is detected for the third time with the same fault code, with no detection of a different fault code between the first and the third detection and without 60 s of fault-free operation since the first of these detections, the controller shall latch the safe state until a power-on reset.
items.rationale: Reworked for CON-SUP-117, which reads the three consecutive resets of CON-SUP-110 as the third detection: the first and second detections lead to a reset, the third latches without a reset. CON-SUP-110 requires the resets to be consecutive with the same fault code, so a detection of a different fault code (and its reset) between the first and third detection breaks the sequence and the latch condition is not met.

items.text: The supervisor shall keep the safe-state latch and the fault history in memory that survives software resets and watchdog resets.
At start-up, the supervisor shall classify the reset cause from the reset flags as power-on, independent watchdog, window watchdog, supervisor reset or other.
At start-up, the supervisor shall send the classified reset cause in a start-up message on the diagnostic serial line.
When the classified reset cause is independent watchdog or window watchdog, the supervisor shall send a fault report with fault code 8.

When the request GET STATUS is received on the diagnostic serial line, the supervisor shall return STS,<state>,<fault count> within 50 ms, with <state> one of STARTUP, OPERATIONAL, SAFE or LATCHED, selected as defined in SYS-SUP-051, and <fault count> the number of fault reports since the last power-on reset, which is kept across software and watchdog resets.
items.rationale: Updated for CON-SUP-125 (answer to part of former OP-SYS-005).

items.text: When the request GET FAULTS is received on the diagnostic serial line, the supervisor shall return the last 8 fault reports within 50 ms.

When the request GET RESET is received on the diagnostic serial line, the supervisor shall return RST,<cause> within 50 ms, with <cause> one of POR, IWDG, WWDG, SW or OTHER, the classified reset cause.
items.rationale: Added for CON-SUP-118.

items.text: When a request other than GET STATUS, GET FAULTS or GET RESET is received on the diagnostic serial line, the supervisor shall answer ERR.
The supervisor shall use the diagnostic serial line at 115200 baud with 8 data bits, no parity and 1 stop bit.

The supervisor shall use no more than 10 % of the processor time, measured as its execution time over any 1 s window in normal operation without fault and without service request on the simulator at the configured core clock.
The supervisor test build shall provide a test hook that injects each fault class with fault codes 1 to 9.
The supervisor shall exclude the fault-injection test hooks from the production build.
items.rationale: CON-SUP-116 states the hooks exist only in test builds.

items.text: The supervisor shall run on the Renode simulator with the STM32N6 platform description, without the real board.
The supervisor shall use no dynamic memory allocation and no recursion.
While the safe state is latched, the supervisor shall not request a software reset.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-SUP-027. The safe state is latched until a power-on reset by SYS-SUP-043 (fault code 9) and, at the third detection of the same fault code, by SYS-SUP-028 (CON-SUP-117), so no reset is requested there.

items.text: When a configuration fault with fault code 9 is detected, the controller shall latch the safe state until a power-on reset.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-SUP-009 (F-sys-req-item-r2-003). The detection of fault code 9 is stated in SYS-SUP-009; this item states only the latch reaction to that detection.

items.text: While no fault with fault code 1 to 7 or 9 has been detected since the last reset and the safe state is not latched, the supervisor shall service the independent watchdog so that the time from the reset to the first service and the time between any two consecutive services are each less than 100 ms.
items.rationale: Added for F-sys-req-set-r1-008. STK-SUP-005 requires the watchdogs to be serviced while supervised tasks are healthy. The independent watchdog times out after 100 ms (CON-SUP-106), so the service interval must stay below that value. Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r2-012: the obligation now also bounds the first service after the reset and requires continuing service, so no timeout occurs in healthy operation. The condition equals that of SYS-SUP-011 and is the complement of the withholding in SYS-SUP-013.

items.text: After a loss of power, the controller shall start with the safe-state latch not set and without the fault history recorded before the power loss.
items.rationale: Added for F-sys-req-set-r1-011. CON-SUP-110 states the latch and fault history are kept in memory that survives software and watchdog resets but not power loss; SYS-SUP-029 states the survival and this item states the loss.

items.text: While the safe state is latched, including throughout every watchdog reset and software reset, the controller shall hold both control outputs and the status signal low until a power-on reset.
items.rationale: Added for F-sys-req-set-r2-011. SYS-SUP-013 withholds watchdog service while the safe state is latched, so SYS-SUP-010 and SYS-SUP-012 end in resets; CON-SUP-110 keeps the safe state latched until power-on reset. This item states that the outputs and status signal stay low during and after each such reset, not only under the start-up hold of SYS-SUP-020, which ends when the start-up checks pass.

items.text: When a fault with fault code 1 to 7 is detected and the detection does not latch the safe state, the controller shall hold both control outputs and the status signal low from the instant of safe-state entry until the reset that follows.
items.rationale: Added for F-sys-req-set-r3-011. SYS-SUP-022 drives the outputs and status low within 50 ms; SYS-SUP-046 holds them only while the safe state is latched; SYS-SUP-020 holds them from the reset until the start-up checks pass. This item closes the gap in between for an unlatched fault: low from entry until the reset requested under SYS-SUP-027. Updated for CON-SUP-117: at the third detection the safe state is latched and SYS-SUP-046 holds the outputs.

items.text: Unless a watchdog reset occurs first, when a flow fault with fault code 4 is detected at the end of a control cycle, the supervisor shall send one fault report for that control cycle whose entity is the task expected at the first position, in the configured release order of the tasks released in that cycle, at which the received checkpoint differs from the expected one or is missing.
items.rationale: Updated for CON-SUP-123 (answer to former OP-SYS-013, now removed): the checkpoints received in the cycle are compared position by position with the configured release order and the entity is the task expected at the first position where the received checkpoint differs or is missing (example: expected T_IN, T_CTRL; received T_CTRL, T_IN gives T_IN). This covers the out-of-order case and the mixed missing and out-of-order case that earlier versions of this item excluded, and gives the same entity as the earlier missing-only rule when the received checkpoints are in order. History: Added for CON-SUP-122 (answer to former OP-SYS-012): the entity rule for fault code 4, complementing SYS-SUP-026. Rework r7: (1) the watchdog-reset exception matches SYS-SUP-023 and CON-SUP-121: a reset before the report and safe-state entry complete removes the obligation for this fault, which is reported at the next start-up as fault code 8 (SYS-SUP-032). (2) CON-SUP-122 names the first task whose checkpoint is 'missing or out of order' but no approved decision says which task is the out-of-order one when checkpoints arrive swapped (expected A, B; received B, A). The item is therefore limited to the missing-checkpoint case, which is unambiguous; the out-of-order entity rule is recorded as blocking OP-SYS-013 and not invented here. Rework r8 (F-sys-req-item-r8-001): the item applies only when the checkpoints that did arrive are in configured release order. In that case no task has an out-of-order checkpoint, so the first task whose checkpoint is missing is exactly the first task whose checkpoint is missing or out of order, as CON-SUP-122 states; the two rules cannot select different entities. Cycles that contain both a missing checkpoint and checkpoints received out of release order are outside this item and their entity rule is covered by OP-SYS-013.

items.text: The supervisor shall express <ms since start> in each fault report as the milliseconds since the latest reset of any kind, as an unsigned decimal number of 32 bits that wraps to zero after 4294967295 ms.
items.rationale: Added for CON-SUP-126 (answer to former OP-SYS-006).

items.text: The supervisor shall select the <state> value of STS,<state>,<fault count> as follows: LATCHED while the safe state is latched until a power-on reset; SAFE from the completion of a safe-state entry until the next reset, when the safe state is not latched; STARTUP from any reset until the start-up checks have passed, when no safe-state entry has completed since that reset and the safe state is not latched; OPERATIONAL after the start-up checks have passed, when no safe-state entry has completed since the last reset and the safe state is not latched.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-SUP-033 (finding F-sys-req-item-r11-007). CON-SUP-125 gives the four labels; the conditions follow from CON-SUP-109 (start-up until checks pass), CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-115 (latch until power-on reset) and the safe-state entry on fault detection (STK-SUP-009). Reworked for F-sys-req-item-r12-003: the earlier text selected SAFE from fault detection and gave a precedence for a fault during start-up; the sources do not decide either. This text uses completion of safe-state entry (CON-SUP-105, CON-SUP-120), and states the conditions so they do not overlap. Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r8-004: when the latch applies (SYS-SUP-028, SYS-SUP-043), LATCHED is the only value, because the latch is the longer-lived condition (until power-on reset) and SAFE is now stated only for an unlatched safe state. The state reported between detection and safe-state entry, for a fault detected during start-up, and after a code 8 watchdog-reset report (CON-SUP-121; no safe-state entry is made, SYS-SUP-027) is not decided; see OP-SYS-015.

open_points.text: The CRC-32 of CON-SUP-107 and CON-SUP-124 is given only by its polynomial 0x04C11DB7. The initial value, input reflection, output reflection, final XOR and the byte order (endianness) of the 4-byte reference stored at __app_crc (and of the CRC stored with the configuration block) are not given. A decision is needed so the expected result of the start-up and run-time comparisons (SYS-SUP-014, SYS-SUP-015, SYS-SUP-019) is unique.

CON-SUP-125 lists the STS states but no transition rules. A decision is needed for SYS-SUP-051 on three cases: (a) the state a GET STATUS answer carries between fault detection and completion of safe-state entry, which CON-SUP-105 and CON-SUP-120 allow to be up to 50 ms; (b) the state for a fault detected during start-up before the checks have passed; (c) the state after a start-up that reports a code 8 watchdog-reset fault (CON-SUP-121), where no safe-state entry is made.

The request framing (terminators, case, whitespace) and the start-up message format are not given in CON-SUP-111 and CON-SUP-113; the values of <state> and the meaning of <fault count> are decided in CON-SUP-125.
The configured core clock value used for the processor-time measurement of CON-SUP-114 is not given.
